<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Deuteronomy 32:1">Targ. Y. Deut. XXXII, 1</cite> <he>דלא טַעֲמִין מיתותא</he> which taste no death (heaven and earth).—
<cite ref="Berakhot 44a:3">Ber. 44ᵃ</cite> <he>דלא ט׳ זיונא</he> that he tasted no food.
<cite ref="Shabbat 11a:7">Sabb. 11ᵃ</cite> <he>לִיטְעוֹם מר מידי</he> take some refreshment, Sir!—
<cite ref="Horayot 11a:19">Hor. 11ᵃ</cite> <he>אִטְעוֹם טעם דאיסורא</he> I wish to try how a forbidden thing tastes; a. fr.

<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 1:3:1">Koh. R. to I, 3</cite> <he>לית את מַטְעַם לי מתבשילי</he> wilt thou not let me taste what I have cooked (for thee?); <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 28:3">Lev. R. s. 28</cite>; <cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 18:1">Pesik. R. s. 18</cite>; Pesik. Haomer, p. 70ᵃ … <he>מַטְעִים … מתבשילך</he> of the dish prepared for thee?

senses.gloss: to taste. Part. pass. מְטַעַם tasted, touched. Lev. R. l. c. why do the dishes come out ולא מְטַעֲמִין without being touched?; (Koh. R. l. c. ולא טעמין and they taste them not).
